candidates.name: eu-visa-policy
candidates.what_it_holds: visitor-visa-statistics.csv: EU/Schengen short-stay visitor visa applications, issuances and refusals by member state, 2005-2022, built from the Council Document Register (2005-2008) and the EU Migration and Home Affairs Commission website (2009-2022); World Bank income/region classification joined on for country grouping; 88 commits; Python build scripts (program.py, geography.py, create-output-datasets.py); core dataset also mirrored on Kaggle
candidates.why_useful: This is actual Schengen visa-statistics time series (applications/issued/refused by country, 2005-2022) — directly answers the theme's core ask and nothing like it is in our current holdings (gap 7/12 adjacent: cross-border demand and regulation). Could proxy inbound EU short-stay demand trend and correlate with EMEA nights.
candidates.license: not stated in README (check repo root for LICENSE file before use)
candidates.last_activity: not confirmed via fetch; 88 commits, appears mature/complete project
candidates.size_hint: one core CSV + derived aggregate CSVs; row count not confirmed

candidates.name: passport-index-data
candidates.what_it_holds: 7 files (1 JSON + 6 CSV: matrix/tidy x name/ISO2/ISO3) of visa requirements for 199 countries x 199 destinations (visa-free days, visa-free, visa-on-arrival, eTA, e-visa, visa-required, no-admission); actively maintained, most recent data dated 17 Feb 2026; MIT licensed; 83 stars, 4 commits; explicitly the maintained continuation of ilyankou/passport-index-dataset which is now archived (last updated 12 Jan 2025)
candidates.why_useful: Currency of a passport/visa-openness index is a proxy for ease of cross-border travel by nationality pair; can be joined with regional nights mix (gap 7/20) to test whether visa-liberalization events move bilateral travel flows into ABNB's regional splits. This is the live successor to the widely-cited but now-archived ilyankou repo.
candidates.time_coverage: current snapshot only (no historical panel in this repo)

candidates.name: indice-movilidad-visamundial (IMV)
candidates.what_it_holds: ranking-imv.csv (199 passports, IMV mobility scores + category breakdown of visa-free/on-arrival/eTA/e-visa/required/denied), matriz-tidy.csv (39,402 passport-to-destination pairs, 3 columns), indice-movilidad.json; version 2026.2 (6 Aug 2026), quarterly-reviewed, cross-verified 3,714/3,852 pairs against US State Dept/Canada IRCC/EU Commission/national foreign ministries, corrected 108 misclassifications versus the base matrix; base matrix sourced from imorte/passport-index-data; CC-BY 4.0
candidates.why_useful: A currently-maintained (Aug 2026), independently verified global visa-mobility index with an explicit methodology note distinguishing visa-free/eTA/e-visa access — more rigorous than a raw passport-index mirror and usable as a cross-border ease-of-travel covariate by origin-destination pair, relevant to gap 20 (cross-border share proxies) and regional mix work.
candidates.time_coverage: current snapshot, versioned quarterly since some earlier date

candidates.name: canadian-border-crossings-analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: data/ folder with BTS monthly inbound US-Canada land-border crossing counts by port (1996-present), a Border Policy Research Institute passenger-vehicle intercept survey at Whatcom County crossings (31,208 individual responses across 4 waves: Summer 2018, Winter 2019, Summer 2025, Winter 2026), and NTTO air-passenger arrivals data Jan 2019-Jul 2026; scripts/ for the analysis; figures/; MIT license; 15 commits, active through 2026
candidates.why_useful: Direct hit on gap 10 (BTS border-crossing data) with committed BTS series plus something we don't hold at all: a point-in-time individual-level cross-border traveler survey (2018-2026, 4 waves) and NTTO air arrivals extending into 2026 — could sharpen the US-Canada leisure travel read for the North America regional split.
candidates.geography: US-Canada land border, multiple states/provinces (Vermont, North Dakota, New York, Washington)

candidates.name: north-america-border-crossing-dashboard
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: same underlying data.gov BTS Border Crossing Entry Data series as AlexBogden/canadian-border-crossings-analysis above, packaged only as a Power BI file rather than raw CSV
candidates.what_it_holds: dashboard.pbix (Power BI file, hosted on Google Drive due to size) built on the data.gov 'Border Crossing Entry Data' series, covering US-Canada and US-Mexico borders 1996-2025 by state/port; MIT license; 2 commits
candidates.why_useful: Confirms the BTS Border Crossing Entry Data series (1996-2025, both US-Canada and US-Mexico, state/port level) as a public, easily citable source, though this particular repo does not commit the raw CSV itself (only a Power BI binary on Google Drive) so it's lower priority than the AlexBogden repo above.
candidates.geography: US-Canada and US-Mexico borders, all states

candidates.name: nakordoni developer API docs
candidates.what_it_holds: OpenAPI spec + code samples for nakordoni.eu's commercial API: real-time and historical border-queue lengths/wait estimates at European (mostly Ukraine-EU and intra-EU) truck/car checkpoints, ML 24h/7d queue forecasts, hourly/daily historical stats per checkpoint, plus adjacent European fuel-price, POI, road-condition and toll data; sourced from national road authorities, TomTom/HERE, crowd reports; free-tier requires email registration; last touched 2026-09-13
candidates.why_useful: A live, queryable proxy for European land-border friction/congestion (crossing wait times) that could stand in for cross-border travel intensity in EMEA, complementing Schengen visa-issuance stats; only useful as a 'method' pointer since actual queue data lives behind their API, not committed to the repo.
candidates.geography: Europe, primarily Ukraine-EU and intra-EU checkpoints
candidates.time_coverage: live + historical stats per checkpoint (span not specified)

candidates.name: thailand-statistics-analyzer
candidates.what_it_holds: a one-command Python tool pulling Thailand's official national-statistics SDMX API across sectors, with an explicit worked example pulling 'International tourist arrivals to Thailand' with time-based filtering/historical comparison; no data files committed; no license stated; 1 commit
candidates.why_useful: Fills part of gap 7 (APAC regional travel volume — Thailand named explicitly) as a ready-made SDMX puller for Thailand visitor arrivals, which we don't currently have a method for.
candidates.time_coverage: whatever the SDMX API exposes historically

candidates.name: windsor-essex (border wait time PWA)
candidates.what_it_holds: border-wait-times.html widget showing live Gordie Howe Bridge / Ambassador Bridge & Tunnel (Windsor-Detroit) wait times, lane status and toll calculator, alongside separate committed JSON scrapes (windsor-events.json, windsor-traffic.json, windsor-news.json, windsor-311.json); source API for the border wait feed not documented; MIT license; 5 commits, updated Aug 2026
candidates.why_useful: Marginal but real: a live front-end consuming a US-Canada bridge crossing wait-time feed at one of the busiest commercial crossings; more useful as a pointer to whatever wait-time API it consumes than as a stored dataset (that source isn't disclosed in the README).
candidates.time_coverage: live only, no historical archive apparent
candidates.size_hint: small JSON scrape files, sizes unknown

candidates.name: borderpatrol (R package)
candidates.what_it_holds: early-stage R package (5 commits, unfinished README, 0 stars) tagged border-patrol/cbp/customs-and-border-protection/illegal-immigration/immigration; package skeleton has data/ and R/ dirs but contents not confirmed via fetch; MIT license
candidates.why_useful: Possible CBP-data R package, but too undeveloped to confirm contents (README description is cut off, no visible data description); flagging only so it isn't missed if it matures, not because it currently demonstrates value.

candidates.name: trusted-traveler-scheduler
candidates.what_it_holds: Python script polling the DHS Trusted Traveler Program (Global Entry/NEXUS) public appointment-availability API for open interview slots; no historical data committed; 61 stars
candidates.why_useful: Not a data source about travel volumes itself, but confirms a public, unauthenticated DHS TTP appointment API exists that a point-in-time scraper could turn into a (weak) proxy for cross-border-traveler enrollment demand/backlog over time; several near-identical sibling repos exist (mvexel/next_global_entry, arun0009/global-entry-slot-notifier, mattpopovich/GlobalEntryChecker) hitting the same endpoint.

notes: WebSearch tool was already at its session-wide 200/200 budget for every query in this session before I could run any (shared across all scout subagents), so no `site:github.com` searches actually executed despite being logged as attempted. WebFetch against Bing/Google/DuckDuckGo search-result pages either rendered generic/empty result sets (Bing dropped the site: filter and just returned github.com's homepage/login/signup) or returned 403 (DuckDuckGo). github.com/search (both the HTML search UI and the API-shaped URL) returned HTTP 429 rate-limited both times I tried it, so likely other scouts are also hammering it. Worked around this entirely by walking github.com/topics/<topic> pages, which render fine, are not rate-limited, and turned out to be a productive substitute for keyword search in this theme, since the true ETIAS/ESTA/eu-visa/schengen-area/border-crossing-data/migration-data/i-94 GitHub topics are literally empty (0 repos tagged) — the topic system undercovers this space, so a next scout on this theme should prefer github.com/search code search (once unrate-limited) or a different search engine, and also try topics: 'nonimmigrant', 'dhs', 'homeland-security', 'schengen-calculator' (all appointment/day-counter tools, already sampled and unhelpful), and Kaggle/Zenodo directly (not attempted this pass — recommend a follow-up scout on Kaggle 'border crossing entry data', 'CBP wait times', 'schengen visa' with dataset search, since data.gov/Kaggle mirrors of the BTS series and any historical Schengen visa Eurostat migr_eirfs table seem more promising there than on GitHub topics). CBP official wait-time API (bwt.cbp.gov) — no GitHub client repo was found for it in this pass; worth another look via code search once available.
